chk.summary:
Final check of merge_vv.md draft v1 (read only, no simulation; code read at c1c 4dfefca, not run). Scripts and outputs: /tmp/claude-1000/-srv-shared-Workspace-phd-phd-speed-harmo-v5b1/2d269ac5-95be-4f04-801b-ec9cc9873355/scratchpad/vvr2/check/ (x1.py to x5.py, x2.out, x4.out), all from my own stream of the 14,880 stored E30 rows.

Verdict: no blocker. v1 fixes most round-1 majors correctly. Two majors remain, both in V3, both fixable with a few lines and no extra runs. About a dozen minors.

(1) Round-1 majors (after skeptic): fixed correctly: D2, D3, D5 (as an author decision), D6, C3, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, B1, B5, B7, C4, C8, and the critic's M1, M2, M4, M7, M8, M9. Partly fixed: D1 and C1 (K1, K2, K13), D7/B6 (K4), B3 (K11), F7 (K14), M3 (K6), M5 (K2), M6 and M10 (K10). No fix introduced a serious new problem; the new issues are the gate now voiding a reading it no longer needs to guard (K3) and a misstated 0/40 bound (K4). Details per finding in K0.

(2) v1 on its own. Numbers that reproduce: the merge-scaling model against lr400_16_1 (+7.29, +4.70, +0.36, -5.63 at k = 0.34, 0.2, 0.1, 0.02; HOLDS about 0.86-0.88, 0.37, 0.02, 0), the 80-85 % merge share, C1 check (a)'s 0.34 and 0.02, +32.1/+21.9/+16.0, the +0.5 (SE 0.35) half-second difference, the +6.2 lower bound, the run rate (1,067 per hour) and the cost line (about 8.1 h, $1.2 before the meter). V2's +/-3 margin has ample power at n = 480 under the ttc_half proxy (SE 0.35: MET about 1.00 for a true difference up to 1.5 points, 0.82 at 2, 0.025 at 3). Levels and null bars agree between section 2 and section 6. Seeds do not overlap and I found no earlier use of 7,492,xxx or 7,493,xxx (decisions.md, both repos, 48 meta.json files in the run folders; not a full scan). Every gate can fail under no effect except where labelled as wiring; exceptions are in K4 and K10. Not reproducible as stated: the 0/40 bound (7.2 % holds for a simple random 40, about 11-12 % for the 20 + 20 draw the plan specifies) and VV-D10's "about +7 %" (7.5-9.6 % at 600 m under the plan's own model).

The two majors: (K1) Q3 promises "the size of the dependence", but no statistic estimates the change of the edge between 300 m and 600 m; the likely NOT SHOWN would be read as "the edge lives where the lanes are short" from a non-significant result. (K2) The expected NOT SHOWN/WORSE is driven by about 25 samples per run on edge 1 during the slowdown hold, not by lane length: without them the same model gives +11.5, +10.3, +8.3, +6.0. The plan labels edge 1 "entry" and does not pre-state this.

(3) Too complex for the question: the per-merge gate that voids the 600-m reading (K3), the visual check of 40 after every sample is already classified by code (K4), V2's printed swap null and NOT INFORMATIVE clause (K8), and V6 with no stop rule (K12).

Limits of this check: the V2 power uses ttc_half against ttc_net as a stand-in for 0.1 s against 1 Hz, which is an assumption; the HOLDS probabilities are a normal approximation plus a 300 x 400 double bootstrap around the stored sample; nothing was measured at 600 m.

findings.title: Round-1 majors: status in v1, one line each
findings.claim: Fixed correctly: D2 (gate statistic defined per merge, 95 % bound, p333 printed), D3 and B5 (meter on the counter's definition, two exact BUG checks, difference statistic with a margin), D5 (n = 480 kept as an author decision with the alternative listed), D6/C3/F1 (V4 descriptive, no verdict, two quantities), F2 (I-80 by lateral crossing), F3 (merge position dropped), F4 (10-s stop share dropped), F6 (VV-D5 with disclosure), B1 (node shift, T0 on the whole lane-length dict), B7/C4 (per-merge gate, vehicle-seconds wording, distinct vehicles), C8 (replication line with both wordings), M1 (Q3b, V6, limit M1), M2 (wording line, encounters), M4 (VV-D7), M7 (VV-D3 B listed), M8 (seed approval request, separate trace block), M9 (reader frozen, read once, frozen worktree). Partly fixed: D1 and C1 (dependence wording and expectation table are in; the paired difference of edges and the edge-1 pre-statement are not: K1, K2, K13), D7/B6 (wiring labelled, same-lane gap rebuilt; cross-lane samples, double counts and the definition of a non-event are missing: K4), B3 (remap fixed; the input-distribution print is dropped: K11), F7 (merge log has types and rebuilt gaps; follower split and instant mismatch not stated: K14), M3 (prints added; the fixed sentence is wrong about braking: K6), M5 (groups fixed, edge-1 samples traced; pre-statement missing and the label presumes the cause: K2), M6 (V7 added; its criterion and the V462 consequence do not hold as written: K10), M10 (section 6 exists; limits and PR status per row, and how NOT REPLICATED combines with the 600-m reading, are missing: K12). Not fixed, minor in round 1: D10 (K7), the second half of D9 (K1), D11's period split (K10).
findings.evidence: docs/research/protocols/merge_vv.md against docs/research/results/merge_vv/review_r1/findings.json (severity_after and better_fix per finding) and docs/research/protocols/merge_vv_review.md.
findings.fix: None for the fixed ones. See K1-K14 for the rest.

findings.title: V3 promises the size of the dependence but has no statistic for the change of the edge between 300 m and 600 m
findings.claim: Section 0 says V3 gives "the size of the dependence", and the expectation paragraph and section 5 say a NOT SHOWN or WORSE "says the edge lives where the lanes are short". The only readings are a significance test at 600 m (HOLDS / WORSE / NOT SHOWN). A NOT SHOWN at 600 m beside a shown edge at 300 m does not show that the edge changed. Round 1 asked for this (D9's skeptic: any statement of change between lengths uses the paired difference of the two edges on the same seeds, with its interval); the handling table took only D9's first half.
findings.evidence: Under the plan's own model at k = 0.2 the 600-m edge is +4.70 (SE 2.45), read NOT SHOWN about 63 % of the time, while the change from +9.93 is 5.2 points. If the two lengths were independent the SE of the change would be about 3.1 points (from SE 1.93 and 2.45; x2.out block 3), so that change would not be resolved. How much pairing by seed helps cannot be computed from the stored rows (an unknown, not a number). At k = 0.34 the change is 2.6 points.
findings.fix: Add one pre-registered line to V3b: the 600-m edge minus the 300-m edge on the same seeds (C-D5 form, seeds resampled jointly, 95 % interval), against each rule. Put it in every record sentence ("at 300 m a %, at 600 m b %, change c [lo, hi]"). Change the NOT SHOWN wording to say whether the change is itself shown. Delete or soften "says the edge lives where the lanes are short" unless the change's interval excludes 0.

findings.title: The expected NOT SHOWN or WORSE comes from edge-1 samples during the slowdown hold, not from lane length; the plan calls edge 1 "entry" and does not pre-state this
findings.claim: The expectation table is right as arithmetic, but its negative end is carried by about 25 samples per run on edge 1 that v3w and p333 have and the lr rules do not. These fall almost entirely in the hold period of the slowdown on edge 2, so they look like vehicles approaching the slowed section, not vehicles just inserted (inference from period keys; position along edge 1 is not stored). The plan's sentence "NOT SHOWN or WORSE is the likely outcome even with a perfect policy; such a reading says the edge lives where the lanes are short" attributes the loss to the lanes. Round 1 (C1's skeptic, M5) asked to say before data that a WORSE carried by edge 1 is not a lane-length effect; v1 fixed the groups and traces the samples but dropped that sentence, and its example ("a vehicle just inserted under a commanded headway") points to the wrong cause.
findings.evidence: x2.out block 2: median edge-1 samples per run 22-25 for the five learners, 25 for p333, 2 for lr400_16_1, 3 for grid_lr400_13_1, 1 for no control. x5.py: mean per run on edge 1 by period, w0u250 24.9 in hold of 25.3, w1u500 25.4 of 25.8, p333 26.1 of 26.7; lr400_16_1 2.8, grid 3.2, no control 1.7. x2.out block 3: model against lr400_16_1 with edge 1 included +7.29, +4.70, +0.36, -5.63 (k = 0.34, 0.2, 0.1, 0.02); with edge-1 samples left out +11.50, +10.25, +8.28, +5.95 (97.5 % lower ends +6.8, +5.1, +3.1, 0.0).
findings.fix: Rename the group "edge 1 (upstream of the slowdown)". Add both rows to the expectation table. Pre-state: "a WORSE or NOT SHOWN carried by edge 1 is the approach to the slowdown, not a lane-length effect", and fix how "[where]" is filled (the group with the largest deficit in samples per run). Print, not deciding, the 600-m edge without edge-1 samples beside the deciding one. In V1 describe edge-1 samples by period and position along the edge instead of presuming insertion.

findings.title: The lane-end standing gate now voids a reading it no longer needs to guard; its 80 % bar is not an author decision
findings.claim: The gate was built for "artefact removed". V3 is now worded as dependence on lane length, and "with 600-m lanes the policy still spent less time below 3 s TTC" is true or false whatever the standing did. If neither merge passes, 4,320 runs produce NOT INFORMATIVE although the edge at 600 m and the measured cut are a valid answer to Q3. The gate needs the 95 % lower bound of the cut at or above 80 % for each of 4 arms at a merge; the only evidence is one point value in another cell (no control at merge 2 in S: 526.5 to 48.5, 90.8 %), and nothing for merge 1. Round 1's cheap early look (stop counts at 600 m on the smoke seeds, so the author can decide before the bulk run) was dropped without a note. The gate itself is sound as a test: it fails under no effect.
findings.evidence: No-effect behaviour, x2.out block 7: random halves of one arm give cuts between -0.45 and +0.31 at merge 1 and between -0.33 and +0.24 at merge 2, so 80 % cannot arise by chance. docs/research/results/c1/checks.json: end_stop2 526.5 to 48.5 (no control), 549.5 to 3.5 (p333) at 595 m in S. E30 medians at 300 m: merge 1 136.5-256.5, merge 2 417.5-901 vehicle-seconds per run.
findings.fix: Simplest: make the cut a reported number, not a gate. Every 600-m sentence carries "lane-end standing fell by x % at merge 1 and y % at merge 2 [intervals]", and HOLDS is worded "with standing removed" only for merges whose lower bound is at least 80 %. If the gate is kept, list the 80 % bar and the 95 % level as a decision, state the null above in the plan, and have the smoke print the 600-m standing counts for the author before the bulk run.

findings.title: V1: the 0/40 bound is misstated for the planned draw, "non-event" is undefined, and cross-lane samples and double counts have no check
findings.claim: (a) "0 of 40 bounds the non-event share below about 7 %" holds for a simple random sample of 40. The plan draws 20 in the merge area and 20 elsewhere, while the merge area holds 80-85 % of samples; the bound on the overall share is then about 11-12 %, above the 9.9 % edge. (b) The plan never says what makes a plotted sample a non-event, so the criterion has no defined way to fail. (c) The gap check covers same-lane samples only; samples whose leader is on the next edge or in a junction, and double counts of one follower in one second, have no check and no printed share, although D7's and B6's skeptics asked for both with a zero-tolerance class. (d) "TTC from the log < 3 s" recomputes from the tracer's own log, so it is a wiring check listed under definition checks. (e) The new main-lane and encounters counters are not recounted from the trace, although one of them feeds a pre-registered reading (V283 rule).
findings.evidence: x2.out block 5: 0 of 40 gives 7.22 %; 0 of 20 gives 13.9 %; stratified 20 + 20 with merge share 0.80-0.85 gives 11.1-11.8 %. Junction samples are 1.0-1.7 % of each arm's count (x2.out block 2).
findings.fix: Draw the 40 as a simple random sample (or state 14 % per stratum). Define a non-event in one line (for example: leader not ahead on the follower's lane or its next lane, or gap not closing). Add two by-code classes with a criterion: leader not on the follower's lane or the next lane of its route (share printed, visual sample drawn from these first) and double count (must be 0). Move the TTC recomputation to the wiring list. Add: main-lane count and encounters in the row equal their recount from the trace. Or, to simplify, drop the visual check and keep the by-code classes with these two criteria.

findings.title: "Equal on every key" cannot hold and contradicts V519; a failure is labelled BUG
findings.claim: V1's wiring check and section 3's identity replay require stored-seed runs to equal their stored rows "on every stored key" / "on every key". Stored rows hold run metadata that will always differ (wall_s, commit, files), and V519 fixed the rule for learned policies: traffic values equal, network diagnostics within a tolerance. As written, the check fires a BUG, whose consequence in section 6 is an E30 re-run.
findings.evidence: Stored row keys include wall_s, commit, files, ctrl_sha256, c1_t0 (x3.py, keys.json). docs/decisions.md V519: only m_dec_entropy_mean differed across CPU models, about 1 part in 10^8; "Future identity tests for learned policies: traffic values equal, network diagnostics within a tolerance". The plan allows another instance type "if the rental must split".
findings.fix: Word both checks as cf_ident did: equal on every traffic key (name the key list or the reader function), metadata excluded, policy diagnostics within V519's tolerance. Say that a traced-not-equal-untraced result is a tracer bug that re-runs nothing in E30.

findings.title: The fixed "trained on the metric" sentence is wrong about braking, and the braking number is left out
findings.claim: The sentence says TTC below 3 s is a reward term and "the shorter thresholds and DRAC ... are not separate terms". The reward also has a hard-braking term, so of the four printed measures only DRAC (sev3) lies outside rewarded events: ttc2 and ttc15 are subsets of the TTC term and b45_step is a subset of the braking term. M3 asked for a sentence saying which measures lie outside the reward. The post hoc figures give three numbers for four measures; the missing one is the weak one.
findings.evidence: v5b/fleet/b_env.py:808-847 at 4dfefca: hard = acceleration <= -HARD_BRAKE (3.0 m/s2, line 32); reward term -w_safety * (ttc + hard + 0.5 * (follower ttc + follower hard)). x2.out block 6, against lr400_16_1: ttc2 +32.1 [+26.4, +37.1], ttc15 +21.9 [+17.1, +27.2], sev3 +16.0 [+11.7, +21.3], b45_step +2.4 [-0.6, +5.0].
findings.fix: Fixed sentence: "TTC below 3 s and braking harder than 3 m/s2 are terms of v3w's training reward; TTC below 2 s and 1.5 s and braking beyond 4.5 m/s2 are subsets of those events; only DRAC is outside the reward". Add b45_step's +2.4 [-0.6, +5.0] to the post hoc list.

findings.title: HOLDS still says "the two closest rules" (D10 not fixed); the rules are not tuned for 600 m either; "REPLICATED" covers 2 of 14 competitors
findings.claim: grid_lr400_13_1 is not the second closest rule by point edge: 3ex2, a competitor, is closer, and three trade-point arms are closer still. It is second only by lower bound, by about 0.4 points. Only 2 of 26 non-learning arms run at 600 m, so another rule may be closest there. D10 asked for named rules, both lengths and that disclosure; none is in the HOLDS sentence. WORSE carries the policy's handicap (remapped, geometry not seen); HOLDS carries nothing about the rules, which were picked on 300-m geometry and get new bins. The replication line tests 2 of E30's 14 competitors and no chords but reads plain REPLICATED.
findings.evidence: x2.out block 1 and docs/research/results/cf/screen.json readings: lr400_16_1 +9.93 [+6.16, +14.97]; 3E-C_TRUCK +20.46 (trade point); no control +20.66; 3ex2 +21.25 [+17.96, +24.58] (competitor); 3ex1 +21.54; grid_lr400_13_1 +22.76 [+17.52, +27.14].
findings.fix: HOLDS sentence: "with 600-m lanes v3w still spent less time below 3 s TTC than lr400_16_1 and grid_lr400_13_1 (x %, y %; at 300 m on the same seeds a %, b %); the other 24 arms were not run at 600 m; neither the policy nor the rules were tuned for 600-m lanes". Replication wording: "replicated against lr400_16_1 and grid_lr400_13_1 (2 of 14 competitors, no chords)". In VV-D2 say why these two (smallest lower bounds, closest away from the merges).

findings.title: V2: the margin has ample power, but VV-D9's reason, the printed swap null and the NOT INFORMATIVE clause do not fit the statistic
findings.claim: The design is sound and can fail. Loose ends: (a) VV-D9 says a narrower margin "needs more seeds"; under the stored-row proxy a +/-1.5 margin still reads MET about 0.98 of the time when the true difference is 0, so +/-3 is a choice, not a need. With +/-3 a true loss of 2 points (a fifth of the +9.9 edge) reads MET about 0.8 of the time per rule. (b) A swap null is printed with no bar and no role; an equivalence test's error rate is the 2.5 % at the margin, which the interval already gives. (c) Section 6 makes V2 NOT INFORMATIVE if the 1-Hz edge is not shown; that came from the old criterion. A difference of edges inside +/-3 is informative whatever the edge is, and the text does not say whether the clause overrides MET. (d) "The share of 0.1-s close-following time the 1-Hz count misses" has no formula. (e) No MET sentence is fixed.
findings.evidence: x2.out block 4: ttc_half edge minus ttc_net edge +0.50 (SE 0.35) against lr400_16_1 and -0.26 (SE 0.36) against grid_lr400_13_1; per-run correlation 0.9991-0.9996. x4.out: with SE 0.35, P(95 % interval inside +/-3) = 1.000, 1.000, 0.990, 0.815, 0.025 for a true difference of 0, 1, 1.5, 2, 3; inside +/-1.5: 0.980, 0.815 (at 0.5), 0.298 (at 1), 0.025 (at 1.5). Even at three times the proxy SE, +/-3 reads MET 0.60-0.65 at a true 0. The proxy is an assumption: both are 1-Hz counts half a second apart, not 0.1 s against 1 Hz.
findings.fix: VV-D9: state the power numbers and offer +/-2 as the tighter option (MET 1.00 at 0, 0.82 at 1). Drop the swap null from V2 and state the 2.5 % error at the margin. Drop the NOT INFORMATIVE clause or limit it to the LIMIT branch. Define the missed share as (0.1-s time minus 1-Hz count x 1 s) / 0.1-s time. Fix the MET sentence, for example "the edge at 0.1 s is within 3 points of the 1-Hz edge".

findings.title: VV-D10: the resolvable edge at 600 m is understated, and 960 seeds is rejected for the wrong reason
findings.claim: "n = 480 resolves an edge of about +7 % with power 0.9" uses the 300-m SE. Under the plan's own model the 600-m SE is larger, so the figure is about 7.5-9.6 % against lr400_16_1. The alternative (960 seeds) is dismissed because it "still cannot make a NOT SHOWN mean artefact", which no sample size could; its real effect is on the middle case.
findings.evidence: x2.out block 3, against lr400_16_1: SE 1.93 at 300 m (6.8 %), 2.12, 2.45, 2.58, 2.73 at k = 0.34, 0.2, 0.1, 0.02 (7.5, 8.6, 9.1, 9.6 %). At n = 960 by SE / sqrt(2): 5.3-6.8 %, and P(lower bound above 0) at k = 0.2 rises from 0.37 to 0.68 (normal approximation); the other three cases barely move (0.88 to 0.99, 0.02, 0).
findings.fix: State "about 7.5-9.6 % at 600 m under the model (6.8 % at 300 m)". Give the author the real trade: 960 for the 7 deciding arms at 600 m costs about 3,360 more runs (about $0.5 at the stored rate) and matters only if the cut is near k = 0.2. Keeping 480 is still defensible if K1's change statistic is added.

findings.title: V7 can hardly read MET as worded, and section 6 overstates what opens the V462 wording gate
findings.claim: V7 reads MET only if every observation column is available with on-board sensing and ideal V2V within 150 m. Three of the 16 actor columns are roadside or corridor-wide values (the 200-m roadside bin speed, the merge-zone mean speed, the count of vehicles on both acceleration lanes), so the outcome is LIMIT before any inspection unless a roadside feed is part of the stated capability, as it is for the rules. PR-15's own text asks something else: no seed, event timing or future state. Separately, section 6 says "V7 decides whether the V462 gate can open", but V462 also needs PR-28 closed, and this plan keeps limit M1 on it whatever happens. PR-28 also asks for location by period; no period split is in V3's printed list (D11), so it would be post hoc.
findings.evidence: v5b/fleet/b_env.py:903-940 at 4dfefca (columns 12, 13, 15; V2V_RANGE = 150 at line 36; the actor reads local columns only, c_train.py:72, 89). docs/testing/plant_vv_record_v0.md:19 (V462 needs PR-15, PR-24 and PR-28 closed), :55 (PR-15 text), :83 (PR-28: road, period and lane). Read from code, not run.
findings.fix: V7 criterion: each column's source; whether it uses the seed, event timing or a future state (PR-15's test); and which channel it needs (on-board, V2V within 150 m, roadside feed also read by the rules). MET if no column fails PR-15's test; the channels become a stated assumption or a limit. Section 6: "the V462 gate stays shut after this plan because M1 keeps PR-28 limited; V7 removes one of its three conditions". Add the period split to V3's printed list or say PR-28's period part stays open.

findings.title: VV-D7: the input check at 600 m was dropped, so nothing proves the remap is active or that inputs stay in the trained range
findings.claim: B3's and M4's fixes both asked for the per-column input distribution at 600 m against each checkpoint's mean and SD, from the smoke. v1 has the remap and a unit test at 300 m only. The count of vehicles on the acceleration lanes (column 15, capped at 40 vehicles) may sit at its cap with lanes twice as long, and the WORSE wording "geometry not seen in training" has nothing measured behind it. The project's smoke rule asks for a short run proving outputs carry the inputs after a plant change.
findings.evidence: b_env.py:916, 940: n3a = vehicles on 3a_0 plus 4a_0, input min(n3a / 40, 1). Whether it saturates at 600 m is unknown (not measured; the round-1 reviewer marked it an inference too).
findings.fix: Add to the smoke at 600 m: read back columns 0, 1, 14 and 15 for one learner (ranges, share at a clip, mean against the checkpoint's mean and SD), and one assertion that x on 3a and 4a never exceeds the 300-m training range. Print the share of decisions with column 15 at its cap in the 600-m record sentence if it is large.

findings.title: Specification gaps: cap, null details, interval convention, which instrument runs where, combined outcomes, V6 stop rule
findings.claim: (a) Section 4 has a "cap check" but no cap is set anywhere (CF had one as a decision). (b) The swap nulls give bars but not the number of swaps, the re-estimate rule, or what a failed null reads for the replication and main-lane lines; D4's fix asked for 2,000 and 20,000 swaps. With 2,000 swaps a valid null lands above the 0.94 % bar a few percent of the time. (c) "97.5 % lower bound" means the lower end of a two-sided 97.5 % interval in this project (1.25th percentile), which is what the 1.9 % bar matches; the plan does not say so, and "95 % lower bound" for the gate is open to both readings. (d) It is unclear which instruments run in which runs: V4 and V3's "distinct vehicles" need a per-vehicle merge and standing log in the reading runs, while V1 describes the tracer for 30 runs only; "distinct vehicles from the merge log" names the wrong log. (e) Section 6 does not say how NOT REPLICATED at 300 m changes the 600-m and main-lane readings, and gives no limit number or PR status per row (M10). (f) V6 has no stop rule. (g) Section 3 lists twin tests and the identity replay under Build; they are simulations and belong on the rental (V483). (h) Junction samples (1.0-1.7 %) are not assigned to a road group.
findings.evidence: docs/research/protocols/merge_vv.md sections 2-6; c1_confirm.md section 1 (null: 2,000 swaps, re-estimated once with 20,000 above the bar) and CF-D9 (cap $4); review_r1 D4 (read_cf.py: percentiles 1.25-98.75 with bar 0.019, 0.625-99.375 with bar 0.0094 and 20,000 swaps). Mean wall time per run of the 9 arms is 99.4 s against 99.9 s for all 31 (x3.py), so the cost line's rate carries over.
findings.fix: Add a cap to VV-D6 (for example $4 as CF). One line: "nulls as c1_confirm.md section 1; 20,000 swaps for the 0.94 % bar; a failed null reads NOT REPLICATED / not shown". One line defining the interval convention. A small table of instrument by run set. Two rows in section 6 for the combined cases and a limit and PR column. V6: a fixed search (named databases, date, at most N sources) after which it reads NOT INFORMATIVE. Say twins and identity run in the rental's smoke. Put junction samples in "rest".

findings.title: Main-lane sensitivity at 300 m: power unknown, and its stated limit from round 1 is missing
findings.claim: The stored rows hold no per-lane close-following count, so the SE of the main-lane edge, and so the chance that this pre-registered reading can show anything, cannot be computed before the run. Its negative wording ("the edge is shown only with acceleration-lane and ramp samples included") would rest on a not-shown result. C1's skeptic also asked to state that a main-lane edge does not rule out main-lane congestion caused by the short lanes; v1 leaves that out.
findings.evidence: Row keys (keys.json from x1.py): m_road_ttc3 is by road group and period; groups 3a and 4a include the main lanes beside the acceleration lane; there is no key by lane.
findings.fix: Print the main-lane edge with its interval and SE in both wordings, and word the negative case "not shown on main-lane samples alone (x % [lo, hi])". Add the sentence: "a main-lane edge does not rule out main-lane congestion caused by the short lanes; 600 m is the direct test".

findings.title: Project-rule and wording nits in V3's prints, V4 and the decision table
findings.claim: (a) V3's printed list has delay and served flow but not TTT, which CLAUDE.md wants always alongside. (b) V4's plant side is no control alone; the rule against no-control-alone tables is about performance, but the same two quantities for lr400_16_1 and one learner would cost nothing if the merge log is on in those runs. (c) F7's residue: half the followers in a no-control run are ALKS, and v1 does not split the lag gap by follower type or state the mismatch between SUMO's instant lane change and the field's line crossing; the lag time gap has no formula (it is unstable at crawl speeds). (d) The fixed V4 sentence states "congested" and "2005" as facts with no [VERIFY] although the NGSIM documentation is not yet read; "like TET" is a literature term with no source or [VERIFY]. (e) The decision table gives the recommendation and one inferior alternative but no pros and cons of the recommended option, unlike c1_confirm.md and the author's stated format; VV-D6 has no alternative.

findings.claim: Reproduced from my own stream of the stored rows: edge against lr400_16_1 +9.93 [+6.15, +14.91]; merge share of each arm's count 0.803-0.853; model edges +7.29, +4.70, +0.36, -5.63; HOLDS 0.86-0.88, 0.37, 0.02, 0 (the plan's "about 0.3" is at the low end); WORSE 0.23-0.33 at k = 0.02; half-second difference +0.50 (SE 0.35) and -0.26 (SE 0.36); +32.1, +21.9, +16.0; w1u500 is the median learner (1,068.5); 31 / 9 = 3.4; cost 8,710 runs at 1,067 per hour is 8.2 h and about $1.2; about 0.61-0.68 M vehicle-seconds per run, so about 6 M extra lookups for the meter. No-effect behaviour: replication, main-lane and HOLDS read positive at most 1.25 % per rule and need both; WORSE at most 1.25 % over the two rules; V2 reads MET at most 2.5 % when the true difference is at the margin; the gate fails (null cuts within -0.45 to +0.31); the meter and wiring checks are exact; V4 has no verdict by design; V5 has three outcomes; V6 falls back to NOT INFORMATIVE. Seeds: readings 7,492,000-479, traces 7,493,000-019 and stored 7,489,160-161 do not overlap; the highest seed in the run folders' meta.json files is 7,490,959.

verdicts.reason: In the plan, V3b has only the HOLDS/WORSE/NOT SHOWN test at 600 m. Q3 promises 'the size of the dependence', and section 5 says a NOT SHOWN 'says where the edge lives'. The 480 seeds are the same at both lengths, so a paired change can be computed, but none is pre-registered. Round-1 D9's skeptic asked for it (findings.json). sqrt(1.93^2+2.45^2)=3.1 reproduces the independent-case SE. The record sentence 'not shown with 600-m lanes' is neutral on its own. The problem is that Q3 has no statistic behind it and the interpretation text in the expectation paragraph and section 5 reads one in.
verdicts.better_fix: The K1 fix is already light. Add one printed line to V3b: the paired change (600-m edge minus 300-m edge, same seeds, seeds resampled jointly, 95 % interval) against each of the two rules, carried in every record sentence. Q3 is answered only from that interval. Delete 'says where the edge lives' from section 5 and from the expectation paragraph unless the change's interval excludes 0.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced with my own stream and rng (skeptic/s1.py, s2.py). Edge-1 samples per run in the hold period are 23.4-26.2 for the five learners and 26.1 for p333, against 2.8 (lr400_16_1), 3.2 (grid) and 1.7 (nc). The slowdown is on edge 2 (cell_spec). The model against lr400_16_1 gives +7.29/+4.70/+0.36/-5.63 with edge 1 and +11.50/+10.25/+8.28/+5.95 without it (lower ends +6.6/+5.0/+3.1/-0.1). The plan's 'NOT SHOWN or WORSE is the likely outcome even with a perfect policy' is therefore wrong under its own model: a policy without the edge-1 deficit would read HOLDS at k >= 0.1. 'Upstream of the slowdown' is also an inference, though. Periods are time windows and position along edge 1 is not stored, so insertion is not excluded. The rename would presume a cause, just as the plan's 'just inserted' example does.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the neutral label 'edge 1'. Do not rename it 'upstream of the slowdown'. Pre-state: 'a WORSE or NOT SHOWN carried by edge 1 is not a lane-length effect; edge 1 is unchanged at 600 m'. Strike 'even with a perfect policy'. Add the without-edge-1 row to the expectation table. Print the 600-m edge without edge-1 samples beside the deciding one, as a non-deciding line. In V1, describe edge-1 samples by period and lane position without naming a cause.

verdicts.reason: These facts check out. The 80 % bar is in no decision row. D2's skeptic asked to print 600-m standing counts on the smoke seeds, and v1 dropped this without a note. checks.json gives nc 526.5 to 48.5 at SL600, but 526.5 to 523.0 at SL450, so the cut is steep in lane length and is unknown for merge 1. The gate also fails under no effect (null cuts within about +/-0.45). The claim that the gate 'no longer needs to guard' anything is overstated. If standing is not removed, a HOLDS cannot be read as 'the edge survives without short-lane standing'. So the gate still protects the meaning of HOLDS, though voiding NOT SHOWN/WORSE is heavier than needed.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the cut as a printed number per merge with its 95 % lower bound in every 600-m sentence. Word HOLDS 'with lane-end standing removed at merge m' only for merges at or above 80 %. Otherwise drop that clause instead of voiding V3b. Print 600-m standing for nc and lr400_16_1 on the smoke seeds for the author before the bulk run. Add the 80 % bar to the decision table.

verdicts.reason: (a) Confirmed: 0 of 40 gives 7.2 % only for a simple random sample. With 20 + 20 and a merge share of 0.80-0.85, the bound on the overall share is about 11-12 %, and 13.9 % per stratum. (b) Confirmed: 'non-event' is never defined. (c) Cross-lane samples: confirmed. The definition check covers same-lane samples only, and B6's skeptic asked for the next-lane check and its share. Double counts: weak. The counter loops getIDList once per step (b_env.py:803-819 at 4dfefca), so one follower cannot count twice in one step, and the 'logged samples equal ttc_net' wiring check already ties the tracer to the counter. (d) A labelling nit. (e) Confirmed: the main-lane count feeds a reading but is not recounted from the trace.
verdicts.better_fix: Draw the 40 as a simple random sample, or state the bound as about 14 % per stratum. Define a non-event in one line. Add one by-code class: leader not on the follower's lane or the next lane of its route (must be 0; share of next-lane samples printed). Extend the wiring check to 'main-lane count and encounters equal their recount from the trace'. No double-count class is needed.

verdicts.reason: Stored rows hold wall_s, commit, files, ctrl_sha256 and the m_dec_* policy diagnostics (keys.json, 239 keys). V519 found that only m_dec_entropy_mean differs across CPU models, by about 1 part in 10^8, and set the rule 'traffic values equal, network diagnostics within a tolerance'. c1_confirm.md already words identity that way. The plan's 'every key' would literally fire BUG on wall_s, and section 6 makes BUG an E30 re-run. A builder would likely copy the CF wording anyway, so this is minor, not major.
verdicts.better_fix: Replace 'on every stored key' / 'every key' with c1_confirm.md's identity wording (traffic keys equal; provenance and timing excluded; policy diagnostics within V519's tolerance). Add one clause: a traced run that differs from its untraced twin is a tracer bug and re-runs nothing in E30.

verdicts.reason: b_env.py at 4dfefca has hard = acceleration <= -HARD_BRAKE (3.0, line 32), and every reward branch (lines 839-847) subtracts w_safety*(ttc + hard + 0.5*(ft + fh)). The plan's sentence leaves out that braking is rewarded. ttc2 and ttc15 are subsets of the rewarded TTC event, and the round-1 critic itself said so. The post hoc list gives three of the four printed measures. b45_step against lr400_16_1 is +2.4 [-0.6, +5.0] (x2.out block 6), which matches V530's 'not shown'. One caveat: b45_step is measured at step resolution, so it is not strictly a subset of the 1-Hz rewarded samples.
verdicts.better_fix: Sentence: 'TTC below 3 s and braking at 3 m/s2 or harder are terms of v3w's training reward; TTC below 2 s and 1.5 s are stricter versions of the rewarded event and b45_step of the rewarded braking; only DRAC (sev3) is outside the reward.' Add b45_step's +2.4 [-0.6, +5.0] to the post hoc list.

verdicts.reason: screen.json confirms the numbers: 3ex2 +21.25 [+17.96, +24.58], grid_lr400_13_1 +22.76 [+17.52, +27.14], 3E-C_TRUCK +20.46 (trade point). grid is second closest among competitors by lower bound, by 0.44 points. 3ex2 is closer by point edge. V531 already established 'closest rule' for lr400_16_1. 'Two closest rules' is defensible once defined, but the plan never defines it. The disclosures (rules not tuned for 600 m, 24 arms not run, 2 of 14 competitors) are fair and cost one clause each.
verdicts.better_fix: Name the two rules in the HOLDS and REPLICATED sentences instead of 'the two closest'. In VV-D2, define them as the two E30 competitors with the smallest 97.5 % lower bounds. Add 'the other 24 non-learning arms were not run at 600 m; no rule or policy was tuned for 600-m lanes', and 'replicated against 2 of E30's 14 competitors, no chords'.

verdicts.reason: x4.out and x2.out block 4 reproduce the power under the half-second proxy (SE 0.35). But the proxy compares two 1-Hz counts half a second apart. A 0.1-s count can differ from the 1-Hz count systematically if the policy learned the sampling instant, which is the question V2 asks. At three times the proxy SE, +/-3 reads MET only 0.60-0.65 at a true 0. So 'narrower needs more seeds' is not shown false. It is unknown. The other points are real but small. The swap null has no role. The NOT INFORMATIVE clause comes from the old criterion: a difference of edges inside +/-3 still says the sampling loses little. The missed-share formula and the MET sentence are missing.
verdicts.better_fix: In VV-D9, cite the proxy power as an assumption and keep +/-3. Do not add a +/-2 option. Drop the swap null from V2, or state that it is printed only. Remove the NOT INFORMATIVE clause from the V2 row. Define the missed share as (0.1-s time - 1-Hz count x 1 s) / 0.1-s time. Fix the MET sentence: 'the 0.1-s edge is within 3 points of the 1-Hz edge against both rules'.

verdicts.reason: 3.523 x 1.93 = 6.8 % is the 300-m figure. Under the plan's own model the 600-m SE against lr400_16_1 is 2.12-2.73 (my s2.py: 2.14, 2.46, 2.58, 2.72), giving about 7.5-9.6 %. The plan's reason for rejecting 960 ('still cannot make a NOT SHOWN mean artefact') does not bear on sample size. The resolvable edge is a model-based figure, so it should be stated as such.
verdicts.better_fix: Write: 'resolves about +7 % at 300 m and about +7.5-9.6 % at 600 m under the merge-scaling model (an inference)'. Replace the 960 rejection reason with the real trade: about 3,360 more runs (about $0.5) that help mainly near k = 0.2. Keep 480.

verdicts.reason: b_env.py:928-940 at 4dfefca: column 12 is the vehicle's 200-m bin mean speed over all vehicles, column 13 is the merge-zone mean speed, and column 15 counts vehicles on both 3a_0 and 4a_0, which lie more than 1 km apart. Columns 13 and 15 at least need more than V2V within 150 m (V2V_RANGE = 150, line 36). Under V7's wording, LIMIT is nearly certain before any inspection. PR-15 (plant_vv_record_v0.md:55) asks for no seed, event timing or future state, which is a different test. V462 (line 19) needs PR-15, PR-24 and PR-28 closed. PR-28 (line 83) asks for road, period and lane, and V3 prints no period split, so section 6's 'V7 decides whether the V462 gate can open' overstates.
verdicts.better_fix: V7 criterion: MET if no column uses the seed, event timing or a future state (PR-15's own test). List each column's channel (on-board, V2V within 150 m, roadside) as a stated assumption, with roadside columns named as a limit. Section 6: 'V7 can close PR-15; the V462 gate stays shut while M1 and PR-28's period part remain'. Add the period split (existing m_road_ttc3 period keys) to V3's printed list.

verdicts.reason: The plan's smoke list (twins, identity, T0, meter) has no input read-back, and VV-D7 has a unit test at 300 m only. The B3 reviewer and the M4 critic asked for the input distribution at 600 m. B3's skeptic did not. With the remap, columns 0 and 1 are in range by construction once the remap is right, so the real open items are (i) proof that the remap is active at 600 m and (ii) column 15 (min(n3a/40, 1), line 940) possibly sitting at its cap with lanes twice as long. Whether it saturates is unknown.
verdicts.better_fix: In the 600-m smoke, add one assertion that the remapped x on 3a and 4a stays within the 300-m training range. Print the share of decisions with column 15 at its cap. The full per-column mean and SD comparison is optional.
